claim: At an OPEN horizon (every live phase complete, last live phase flagged, no recorded close) no run of either exec driver exits 0 — the parity-notes sentence 'Both exec drivers stop … on EVERY run at an open horizon' taken literally — whatever doctor-driven condition co-occurs with the reached horizon. Concretely, with gate rot on a completed live gate (a criterion of the horizon phase's gate greps a file under $PROJECT_DIR; the pass is criteria-pinned through gate.sh; the file is then deleted): run 1 of hb-exec.js run and of hb exec run stops nonzero, and runs 2, 3 and 4 ALSO exit nonzero with an 'HB-EXEC STOP:' line that names gate_rot or replan_pending — never 'HB-EXEC IDLE: gate_rot_waiting' (or any IDLE line) with exit 0 — identically on both drivers; the backend command is never invoked on any of those runs; and once the file is restored the very next run on each driver is 'HB-EXEC STOP: replan_pending — H2', exit nonzero.
violation: Any driver run after the first at an open horizon with rot printing an HB-EXEC IDLE line or exiting 0; the two drivers differing in exit class on the same run index; a backend invocation (HB_EXEC_CMD='touch INVOKED' leaves a file) on any run; or the post-restore run not stopping on replan_pending. If the drivers are instead meant to idle on rot_waiting at an open horizon, the parity-notes 'on EVERY run' sentence is then false as written and falsifies this constraint in its place.

claim: The stop-on-every-run branch is keyed on the sleep reason replan_waiting alone, and the stop is lifted by exactly the two sanctioned moves, with the once-flag's lifecycle mirrored on both ticks. (a) Every OTHER non-wake reason keeps its pre-change exit class on a flagged project: mid-plan (H1 done and passed, H2 not started, H2 flagged) a regate declared on GATE_H1 makes both ticks sleep regate_pending_waiting and both drivers print 'HB-EXEC IDLE: regate_pending_waiting' with exit 0; project_complete still prints 'HB-EXEC DONE: project complete' exit 0. (b) After a valid close (hb horizon close --reason …, either runtime) the next driver run on BOTH drivers prints 'HB-EXEC DONE: all phases complete' and exits 0, the one after prints 'HB-EXEC DONE: project complete' exit 0, and .replan-alerted is ABSENT after the first of those runs (the all_done-branch clear). (c) At an open horizon whose .replan-alerted already holds H2 (written by either tick), appending a flagged H3 and running each driver with HB_EXEC_BACKEND=script HB_EXEC_CMD='touch INVOKED' dispatches h3a (INVOKED appears, a task_started event for h3a is appended) and .replan-alerted is ABSENT after that run on both runtimes (the task-branch clear, cross-runtime: a flag written by tick.sh is cleared by tick.py's task branch and vice versa); completing H3 through the CLI then stops both drivers with 'HB-EXEC STOP: replan_pending — H3'.
violation: A regate_pending_waiting (or any non-replan sleep) run exiting nonzero or printing STOP on a flagged project; a post-close driver run exiting nonzero or printing anything but the two DONE lines in order; a stale .replan-alerted surviving the all_done or task branch on either runtime (or cleared by one runtime's branch but not the other's); the appended task not dispatched (no INVOKED, no task_started) because of the stale flag; or the H3 completion stopping with the wrong phase or not stopping.

claim: The hostile-shape normalization (hb-audit.js gateObj / audit.py _gate_obj and the gates-map guard) is a NO-OP on every well-formed plan: for every dag that lints at 0 errors on both lints — every planning/*.dag.json including planning/horizon.dag.json, the seeded template dag under plugin/templates, every tests/fixtures/**/*.json that lints clean, each must-trip and clean dag generated by docs/howto/gate-examples/audit-rules-check.sh, and the tests/horizon.sh t1–t6 shapes — the worktree's hb-audit.js and audit.py produce output IDENTICAL to HEAD's (git show HEAD:plugin/templates/hb-audit.js, and HEAD's py/src tree via git archive) in text mode and in --json (findings in the same order with the same keys and values, the same errors/warns counts, the same exit code), the ONLY permitted difference being the addition of speculative_tail findings — and speculative_tail is absent on every repo planning dag, the seeded template and every suite fixture. The rule-name set derivable from hb-audit.js by audit-rules-check.sh's grep equals the set of F(...) rule literals in audit.py, and audit-rules-check.sh prints AUDIT-RULES-PROVEN:11 with its speculative_tail dag tripping exactly {unguarded_phase, unguarded_phase, speculative_tail} on both runtimes.
violation: Any lint-clean dag whose worktree audit output differs from HEAD's on either runtime beyond an added speculative_tail finding (a changed message byte, a reordered or missing finding, a changed errors/warns count or exit code); a speculative_tail finding on any repo planning dag, the seeded template or a suite fixture; the two runtimes' rule-name sets differing; audit-rules-check.sh printing a count other than 11 or its speculative_tail dag tripping a different rule multiset on either runtime.

claim: 'Hostile shapes … read as EMPTY on both runtimes' is an exact equivalence over the FULL finding object, not just (rule, message): for each hostile value — gates map ∈ {null, [], "G_A", 5}; gate value ∈ {null, "python3 -c 1", [{…}], 5, true}; criteria ∈ {null, "test -f out.txt", {"id":"c1","cmd":"…"}, 7, true} — planted in the tests/horizon.sh t1 shape on the TAIL gate G_C, both audits' --json outputs are equal after sorting findings (every key: severity, rule, phase, message and the extras gate/criterion/tail/cut), the text-mode outputs are byte-identical across runtimes, the exit codes agree, AND both equal the audit of the same dag with the hostile value replaced by its empty counterpart ({} for a gates map or gate value, [] for criteria). The same shapes planted on the HEAD gate G_A make the plan all-unverified and both audits speculative_tail-QUIET, and a hostile criteria ELEMENT inside an otherwise well-formed list ([null], ["s"], [5], [[]], [{}], [{"cmd":5}]) yields identical finding objects on both runtimes with no crash, the phase counting as unverified for speculative_tail iff no sibling element is behavioral.
violation: Any listed shape where the two runtimes' sorted --json findings differ in any key (including severity, phase or an extra such as gate), text output differs by a byte, or exit codes differ; a hostile shape whose findings differ from the empty-replaced dag's on either runtime; a head-gate hostile shape firing speculative_tail; or a hostile criteria element crashing either audit or flipping the phase's verified status between runtimes.

claim: A non-string gate_exit reads identically on both audits, as the parity-notes sentence claims ('a non-string gate_exit … never a crash, never a divergence'): for gate_exit ∈ {5, 0, true, false, "", [], ["G_C"], {"g":"G_C"}, null} on the t1 tail phase PC, both audits agree on the finding COUNT, the rule per phase (ungated vs unguarded_phase vs none), the message BYTES (the rendered gate name included — true/True, [object Object]/{'g': 'G_C'}, G_C/['G_C'] are divergences), the extras, the speculative_tail tail/cut, and the exit code; in particular a value that is truthy in JavaScript and falsy in Python ([]) or vice versa must not flip PC between ungated (error, exit 1) and unguarded_phase (warn, exit 0) across runtimes.
violation: Any listed gate_exit shape on which node and python emit a different number of findings, a different rule for PC, a differing message byte, a different exit code, or a crash on either side; a shape on which one runtime treats the gate_exit as present and the other as absent.

claim: The parity-notes claim that the hostile shapes 'are lint errors' is literally true on BOTH lints: for every shape it names — a non-object gates map (null, [], "G_A", 5), a non-object gate value (null, "python3 -c 1", [{…}], 5, true), a non-array criteria (null, "test -f out.txt", {…}, 7, true) and a non-string gate_exit (5, true, [], ["G_C"], {"g":"G_C"}) — hb-lint.js and lint.py each exit 1 (the error class, not 0 and not a crash exit), print at least one '[<id>]'-prefixed error line, print no Traceback/TypeError/AttributeError/'Cannot read', and agree with each other on exit code for every shape (the dag's other content being the lint-clean t1 shape).
violation: Any named shape that either lint accepts at exit 0 (a gate value that is a string or an array, say), any shape on which either lint crashes instead of reporting an error, or any shape on which the two lints disagree on exit code; equivalently, the parity-notes sentence standing as written while such a shape exists.

claim: The marker is a strict boolean on every RUNTIME surface, not only in lint, and the two runtimes agree on each: with a completed H1→H2 project whose last live phase carries horizon ∈ {1, "true", "yes", [true], {"on":true}} (lint-red, but the runtime never consults lint), both resolvers return all_done with identical keys; both ticks wake all_done (no .replan-alerted is written, the sleep after it is project_complete); both reports print NO 'Horizon:' line and exit 0; both closes refuse in the 'not flagged' class with a nonzero exit and no event; and horizon: false on the last live phase behaves exactly as an absent marker on all four surfaces. Only the JSON literal true flips all four — including when a non-last live phase carries true while the last carries "yes" (all_done, no line, close refused).
violation: Any listed non-boolean value producing replan_pending from either resolver, a replan wake or .replan-alerted from either tick, a Horizon line from either report, or an accepted close (or a close refused with an exception rather than the not-flagged refusal) on either runtime; the two runtimes differing on any of the four surfaces for any value; or horizon: false differing from an absent marker.
